features.name: Rage

rules.text:
Level 1: Rage
You can imbue yourself with a primal power called
Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might
and resilience. You can enter it as a Bonus Action if
you aren’t wearing Heavy armor.
You can enter your Rage the number of times
shown for your Barbarian level in the Rages column
of the Barbarian Features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you
regain all expended uses when you finish a Long
Rest.

While active, your Rage follows the rules below.
Damage Resistance.
You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.
Rage Damage.
When you make an attack using
Strength—with either a weapon or an Unarmed
Strike—and deal damage to the target, you gain
a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain
levels as a Barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage
column of the Barbarian Features table.
Strength Advantage.
You have Advantage on
Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
No Concentration or Spells.
You can’t maintain
Concentration, and you can’t cast spells.
Duration.
The Rage lasts until the end of your
next turn, and it ends early if you don Heavy armor
or have the Incapacitated condition. If your Rage
is still active on your next turn, you can extend
the Rage for another round by doing one of the
following:
• Make an attack roll against an enemy.
• Force an enemy to make a saving throw.
• Take a Bonus Action to extend your Rage.
Each time the Rage is extended, it lasts until the end
of your next turn. You can maintain a Rage for up to
10 minutes.

features.name: Unarmored Defense

rules.text:
Level 1: Unarmored Defense
While you aren’t wearing any armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Constitution modifiers. You can use a Shield and still gain
this benefit.

features.name: Weapon Mastery

rules.text:
Level 1: Weapon Mastery
Your training with weapons allows you to use the
mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice, such as Greataxes and Handaxes. Whenever you finish a Long
Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one
of those weapon choices.
When you reach certain Barbarian levels, you gain
the ability to use the mastery properties of more
kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery
column of the Barbarian Features table.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

Level 2: Danger Sense

perils. You have Advantage on Dexterity saving
throws unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

features.name: Reckless Attack

rules.text:
Level 2: Reckless Attack
You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with increased ferocity. When you make your
first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you Advantage on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next
turn, but attack rolls against you have Advantage
during that time.

features.name: Barbarian Subclass

rules.text:
Level 3: Barbarian Subclass
You gain a Barbarian subclass of your choice. The
Path of the Berserker subclass is detailed after this
class’s description. A subclass is a specialization
that grants you features at certain Barbarian levels.
For the rest of your career, you gain each of your
subclass’s features that are of your Barbarian level
or lower.

features.name: Primal Knowledge

rules.text:
Level 3: Primal Knowledge
You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice
from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1.
In addition, while your Rage is active, you can
channel primal power when you attempt certain
tasks; whenever you make an ability check using
one of the following skills, you can make it as a
Strength check even if it normally uses a different ability: Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception,
Stealth, or Survival. When you use this ability, your
Strength represents primal power coursing through
you, honing your agility, bearing, and senses.

revised_reference_entries: You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1.

When you use this ability, your Strength represents primal power coursing through you, honing your agility, bearing, and senses.

1.name: Rage
1.description: Bonus Action: enter Rage without Heavy armor. Strength attacks gain the Rage damage bonus; Strength checks and saves gain Advantage; Bludgeoning, Piercing and Slashing damage is resisted. Rage prevents spellcasting and Concentration. Attacking an enemy or spending a Bonus Action to extend it maintains Rage through your next turn, up to ten minutes total. Extending an active Rage spends no additional Rage use.

2.name: Danger Sense
2.description: You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws unless you are Incapacitated.

2.name: Reckless Attack
2.description: On your first attack roll of the turn, choose Reckless Attack. Strength attacks gain Advantage until your next turn starts, and attacks against you gain Advantage for the same duration.

3.name: Primal Knowledge
3.description: At level 3, choose one additional Barbarian skill proficiency. While Raging, Primal Knowledge lets you use Strength for Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth and Survival checks.

3.name: Primal Path
3.description: At 3rd level, you choose a path that shapes the nature of your rage from the list of available paths. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th levels.

3.name: Barbarian Subclass
3.description: You gain a Barbarian subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Barbarian levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Barbarian level or lower.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat.html}.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

5.name: Fast Movement
5.description: Starting at 5th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing heavy armor.
